anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly: Physical data model and indexing choices do not match workload access patterns, forcing inefficient access paths regardless of query logic.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Collected statistics are stale or inaccurate, causing systematic cardinality misestimation and misguided plan costing.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level memory, I/O, parallelism, and background-worker settings are mis-tuned for the hardware and workload, so resources are under- or over-utilized.

When all three root causes coexist, the workload may display extreme and erratic performance swings: queries oscillate between full-table scans mandated by poor indexing and bad estimates, while memory or parallelism limits chosen by misaligned parameters cause frequent plan spills, excessive temp-space use, or runaway parallel workers. Autotuned features repeatedly recompile plans yet fail to stabilize them, leading to plan-cache churn, CPU spikes, and I/O storms that are disproportionate to actual user demand. Write operations suffer both from oversized or redundant indexes and from aggressive checkpoint or log-flush settings, resulting in vacillating latency and lock contention. Monitoring views show contradictory signals—e.g., low buffer-cache hit ratios alongside idle disks, or high CPU wait events despite ample headroom—making the anomaly hard to diagnose.

Causally, a flawed schema forces the optimizer to rely heavily on statistics to salvage performance, but stale or missing statistics misdirect it toward even worse plans, hiding the need for better indexes. Misconfigured parameters then amplify every poor plan choice: inadequate work memory turns misestimated hash joins into spill-heavy temp sorts; over-aggressive parallelism magnifies the cost of full scans spawned by missing indexes; too-small buffer pools inflate I/O generated by inefficient access paths. Conversely, throttled background maintenance delays statistics refresh and index maintenance, feeding back into the design and statistics problems. The intertwined feedback loops escalate resource waste, degrade throughput, and obscure the primary culprits, producing a severe, multifaceted performance regression across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: Fatal error: Out of memory while loading mysql.time_zone_leap_second table
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with insufficient memory headroom, buffer pressure, oversized intermediate state, or memory-allocation constraints inside the engine or client library.
entry.solution_guidance: Check memory availability, per-session memory settings, large sorts or hashes, and whether workload concurrency is amplifying memory consumption.
